Example Front Company, a name used in fake job interviews

Front Company

No real company, person or product was found behind this name.

Reported 3 times, evidence reviewed on 2026-11-02

Also seen as: Example Front Co, EFC Hiring

A recruiting company with no trace outside its own website. It sends candidates a meeting app to install before a video interview.

What to do now

If you were sent code, a repository or an app to run as part of an interview like this, do not install or run it. Before your call lists what to do instead.

Evidence reviewed

Three candidate submissions were reviewed: the recruiter messages, the meeting invitation and the hash of the installer, compared with the cited vendor analysis.

What was checked

  • No company register in the countries named on its website lists this name.
  • Its website went online eleven days before the first report.
  • None of the staff it names could be found outside its own pages.

Related names

  • Avery Exampleton (name used by the campaign, possibly a stolen identity) Front 2026-11-01

What happened

The recruiter wrote on a messaging app and offered a well-paid remote role. Before the interview, the candidate was asked to install a meeting app from hxxps://frontco-meet[.]pages[.]example/join/candidate. The installer FrontCoMeet-Setup[.]exe matches the first hash above.
